classification.difficultyReason: Use equal angles opposite equal sides and the triangle angle sum to determine two unknown angles in varied orientations.

content.prompt:
Determine the value of the unknown angles in these triangles.
You do not need to show working out.

spec.description: Upright schematic triangle with a horizontal base, matching single ticks on the sloping sides and 120° at the top.
spec.mathematics: The two unlabelled base angles are equal; their sum is 60°.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the given 120° is visible; both unknown angles remain unlabelled.

answer.worked:
The base angles are equal because they are opposite equal sides. Let each be $x^\circ$.
$$\begin{align*}x+x+120&=180\\2x+120&=180\\2x&=60\\x&=30^\circ\end{align*}$$
Both base angles are $30^\circ$.

spec.description: Upright schematic triangle with matching single ticks on its sloping sides and 110° at the top.
spec.mathematics: The two unlabelled base angles are equal; their sum is 70°.

answer.worked:
The base angles are equal because they are opposite equal sides. Let each be $x^\circ$.
$$\begin{align*}x+x+110&=180\\2x+110&=180\\2x&=70\\x&=35^\circ\end{align*}$$
Both base angles are $35^\circ$.

spec.description: Upright schematic triangle with matching single ticks on its sloping sides and 35° at the lower-left vertex.
spec.mathematics: The lower-right angle equals 35°; the top angle is 110°.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the lower-left given is visible; top and lower-right angles are unlabelled.

answer.worked:
The lower-right angle is $35^\circ$ because the base angles of an isosceles triangle are equal. Let the top angle be $x^\circ$.
$$\begin{align*}x+35+35&=180\\x+70&=180\\x&=110^\circ\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Upright schematic triangle with single ticks on the base and right sloping side, and 35° at the lower-left vertex.
spec.mathematics: The top angle equals the lower-left angle because they oppose the marked equal sides; the lower-right angle is 110°.
spec.answerVisibility: Only 35° at lower left is visible.

answer.worked:
The top angle is $35^\circ$ because angles opposite equal sides are equal. Let the lower-right angle be $x^\circ$.
$$\begin{align*}35+35+x&=180\\70+x&=180\\x&=110^\circ\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Upright schematic triangle with matching single ticks on the base and right sloping side, and 40° at lower left.
spec.mathematics: The top angle is 40° and the lower-right angle is 100°.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the given lower-left angle is visible.

answer.worked:
The top angle is $40^\circ$ because angles opposite equal sides are equal. Let the lower-right angle be $x^\circ$.
$$\begin{align*}40+40+x&=180\\80+x&=180\\x&=100^\circ\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Upright schematic triangle with matching single ticks on the base and right sloping side, and 40° at lower right.
spec.mathematics: The unlabelled top and lower-left angles oppose equal sides and are each 70°.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the given 40° at lower right is visible.

answer.worked:
The top and lower-left angles are equal because they are opposite equal sides. Let each be $x^\circ$.
$$\begin{align*}x+x+40&=180\\2x+40&=180\\2x&=140\\x&=70^\circ\end{align*}$$
Both unknown angles are $70^\circ$.

spec.description: Inverted schematic triangle with a horizontal top side, matching single ticks on the sides meeting at the bottom, and 46° at the bottom.
spec.mathematics: The upper angles are equal and sum to 134°.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the bottom given is visible; both upper angles remain unlabelled.

answer.worked:
The upper angles are equal because they are opposite equal sides. Let each be $x^\circ$.
$$\begin{align*}x+x+46&=180\\2x+46&=180\\2x&=134\\x&=67^\circ\end{align*}$$
Both upper angles are $67^\circ$.
